title: Noise sensitivity derivative bound
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a linear threshold function: there are real weights $a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n$ such that $f(x)$ is the sign of $a_0+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$, with zero assigned the positive sign. For $0<\delta\le 1/2$, let $N_f(\delta)=\bigl(1-\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(1-2\delta)^{|S|}\widehat f(S)^2\bigr)/2$, where $\widehat f(S)$ are the uniform Fourier coefficients of $f$. Then $N_f'(\delta)\le \sqrt{3/2}/\sqrt{\delta}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
